references.text: Jesus repeats the same exhortation after the prayer in Gethsemane: 'Pray that you may not enter into temptation' ([ref:Luk 22:46|Luke 22:46]). This forms a frame (inclusio) around Jesus' struggle in prayer in the garden.

The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says to the disciples: 'Watch and pray that you may not enter into temptation' ([ref:Matt 26:41|Matthew 26:41]). The same exhortation appears in the Gethsemane narrative.
The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus urges the disciples to watch and pray so that they do not enter into temptation ([ref:Mark 14:38|Mark 14:38]).
In the Lord's Prayer, Jesus teaches the disciples to pray: 'Lead us not into temptation' ([ref:Matt 6:13|Matthew 6:13]). The same theme of praying for protection from temptation (πειρασμός).
Luke's version of the Lord's Prayer contains the same petition: 'Lead us not into temptation' ([ref:Luk 11:4|Luke 11:4]). The word πειρασμός connects these two texts.

Paul writes that God is faithful and will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear, but with the temptation also provide a way out so that you may be able to endure it ([ref:1 Kor 10:13|1 Corinthians 10:13]). Prayer and watchfulness are the path to avoiding falling into temptation.

Just before this, Jesus tells Peter that Satan has demanded to have the disciples sifted like wheat, but that Jesus has prayed for him ([ref:Luk 22:31-32|Luke 22:31-32]). The exhortation to pray in verse 40 is directly linked to this warning about Satan's attack.
Jesus can help those who are tempted because he himself was tempted ([ref:Hebr 2:18|Hebrews 2:18]). Jesus' own struggle in prayer in Gethsemane shows his solidarity with people who face temptation.

Peter exhorts: 'Be sober-minded and watch! Your adversary, the devil, prowls around like a roaring lion' ([ref:1 Pet 5:8|1 Peter 5:8]). Watchfulness and prayer are necessary to resist temptation – the same lesson Peter himself learned in Gethsemane.

Paul urges believers to 'pray at all times in the Spirit' as part of the spiritual armor ([ref:Ef 6:18|Ephesians 6:18]). Prayer is the central defense against spiritual temptation, just as Jesus exhorts his disciples in Gethsemane.
